Here's what the postmortem and incident threads say:

**What broke** — On Thursday Nov 12, deploy of ingest v2.14.0 (PR ingest#412) raised the default `max_batch_bytes` from 1 MB to 10 MB. With the pods' 512 Mi memory limit, the ingest-worker pods ran out of memory on the first large batch and crash-looped; the change went to all pods at once [1]. Sentry first flagged the OOM at 09:14, 27 minutes after the 08:47 deploy, and there was no consumer-lag alert at the time [1][10]. Kafka brokers were ruled out as the cause [4].

**Customer data** — Nothing was lost. Events kept arriving in Kafka and were processed late; dashboards were stale between 08:47 and 12:27 UTC (3h40), and the Nov 13 reconciliation confirmed event counts per workspace match the Kafka offsets for 08:00–13:00 UTC [1][4]. Maya's incident report to Orbitly says the same: all events received, none lost [2]. Impact was delayed dashboards across all workspaces; 4 customers contacted support (Orbitly, Zest Grocers, 2 trial accounts) [1].

**What's changing** (action items from the postmortem):
1. KES-431 — page on-call when ingest consumer lag exceeds 5 minutes (Noa, due Nov 20) [1][14]
2. KES-432 — ingest config changes go to the canary pool first (Daniel, due Nov 27) [1]
3. KES-433 — raise worker memory limit to 1 Gi and add a load test on batch sizes (Lior, due Nov 27) [1]

Already done: ingest#419 reverted the default to 1 MB, added a memory guard (batcher refuses batches over 25% of the container memory limit), merged Nov 13 [7]. Rollback to v2.13.3 happened at 10:05, with lag fully drained by 12:27 [1].

Side note: Orbitly has formally claimed an SLA credit under section 7 of their MSA [2], and Sam is checking the terms with finance [2][8].
